head: 03d8306
notes: THE RESEARCH REFUTED THE TASK'S OWN THREE OPTIONS BEFORE THE HUMAN SAW THEM, and that is why the question put to them was a different one from the plan's. The plan asked 'is re-ingesting the 21 worth it'; the answer is that re-ingesting CANNOT DO ANYTHING. (1) add_document's duplicate branch (kb/ingest/_documents.py:503-509) returns the existing document and does NOT update filepath, and _generate_doc_id (kb/core.py:2184) is the MD5 of the lowercased, whitespace-collapsed first 10,000 words. MEASURED: text extracted from archive.org's c-hacking-issue-01.pdf yields doc_id cea9b4004347, byte-identical to the doc_id already recorded for c=hacking1.txt. So a re-ingest is a silent no-op - not a duplicate, not a fix. (2) repoint_document (kb/ingest/_documents.py:1980-1988) compares _compute_file_hash (kb/core.py:2238, MD5 of RAW BYTES) against documents.file_hash. Recorded for c=hacking1.txt: d8c01214298c49a1c82b6063f4b2e921. archive.org holds no file with that hash - PDF is 65a6300616086eb6f056dbf6c0b8fee8, _djvu.txt is b1f70da6b93d18ee2c868830b57e4bdf. The original ASCII files are not there in any form. A CORRECTION TO d699884 AND TO MY OWN FIRST READING, worth keeping because both passes nearly made the same mistake: d699884 found the _djvu.txt, and judging the item by that one derived file is misleading in BOTH directions. It looks like a usable full text (it is corrupted OCR - visible '-\ufffd-' where the original has '--', word-set Jaccard 0.486 against the KB text), and it makes the whole item look like a scan. It is not a scan: c-hacking-issue-01.pdf is 19 pages with ZERO embedded images and a clean text layer, i.e. the original ASCII typeset into a PDF, and the _djvu.txt is a round-trip OCR of that generated PDF. WHAT THE 21 ACTUALLY CARRY, measured read-only: 496 chunks, 418 document_entities, 139 document_topics, 58 document_clusters, all card_id NULL. Only the FILE is gone; the text is preserved at higher fidelity than anything archive.org can supply. TWO REAL OPTIONS WERE DECLINED AND THE COSTS ARE THE REASON: force-repointing would override the MD5 guard the plan carries a standing hazard against and bind .txt-typed records to .pdf files for no gain (the PDFs have zero embedded images, so figure OCR gets nothing); remove-and-re-add would discard 615 derived rows to regain a file nothing currently needs. WHAT REMAINS IS ONE DOCUMENTATION TASK, mode flipped to subtask: record the refutation in TO-DOS.md so the re-ingest option is not proposed a third time. touches NARROWED - rw:knowledge_base.db drops to r: and kb/ingest is no longer read, because nothing is ingested. NOTHING WAS INGESTED, DOWNLOADED INTO THE REPO, OR WRITTEN TO THE DATABASE: the PDF probed during research went to the session scratchpad and the DB was opened read-only throughout.
